title: Decision and Gender Biases in Large Language Models: A Behavioral–Economic Perspective

bias_targets.methodology: Eliciting decisions from models using canonical behavioral economics experiments (the Ultimatum Game and the Gambling Game) to estimate parameters for inequity aversion, risk propensity, and loss aversion, and comparing these results to rational economic baselines and human benchmarks.

Using counterfactual identity and pronoun substitution (e.g., 'Joseph, he/him' for male vs. 'Kelly, she/her' for female) in the prompts for the behavioral economics games to evaluate whether systematic differences emerge in the models' inequality aversion, risk propensity, and loss aversion.
